content.value_statement: Late web issues can block launches and harm accessibility, SEO, or core flows. This skill guides browser checks, Lighthouse interpretation, and structured reporting before release.
actual_capabilities: Defines scope for target URLs, viewports, authentication state, and key user flows.
Uses Lighthouse signals for accessibility, SEO, best practices, and performance when relevant.
Guides manual checks for keyboard navigation, focus behavior, contrast, responsive layouts, and forms.
Checks page metadata, headings, image alt text, form labels, ARIA references, and landmarks.
Maps findings to critical, high, medium, and low severity with release priorities.
Requires residual risk notes when manual checks or user flows cannot be completed.
limitations: It is guidance only; it does not bundle Lighthouse, axe, Playwright, or a browser runner.
It cannot certify full WCAG compliance without a formal accessibility audit.
Authenticated or private flows need valid access from the user.
Results depend on the tools and browsers available in the current environment.

use_cases.title: Pre-Release Page Review
use_cases.description: Check a new marketing, signup, or product page before launch for visible accessibility, SEO, and UX blockers.

use_cases.title: Launch Risk Triage
use_cases.description: Turn browser findings into prioritized release decisions with clear evidence, severity, and recommended fixes.

use_cases.title: Accessibility QA Pass
use_cases.description: Combine automated signals with manual keyboard, focus, contrast, form, and ARIA checks on important flows.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a public page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-audit to review this page before deployment: <URL>. Check desktop and mobile widths, then report accessibility, SEO, Lighthouse, and critical UX findings.

prompt_templates.title: Review a User Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate audit of a key journey.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-audit on <URL> for the signup flow. Test keyboard navigation, forms, focus behavior, metadata, console errors, and release-blocking UX issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check Authenticated States
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review that needs provided access.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-audit on the authenticated dashboard after I provide access. Cover desktop, mobile, navigation, dialogs, forms, Lighthouse signals, and residual risk.

prompt_templates.title: Gate a Release Candidate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release decision with strict priorities.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-audit as a release gate for <URL>. Sort findings by P0 to P3, cite evidence, recommend fixes, and state whether deployment should proceed.

output_examples.input: Audit the product page before deployment.
output_examples.output: Browser Audit Summary: desktop and mobile were checked. Verdict: Ready with fixes. Findings include weak focus visibility and missing descriptive image alternatives.

output_examples.input: Review the signup flow for accessibility and SEO blockers.
output: High priority: email input has no programmatic label, which affects screen reader users.
Medium priority: mobile layout creates horizontal scrolling at narrow widths.
Residual risk: payment confirmation was not tested because access was unavailable.

output_examples.input: Run a Lighthouse-focused audit and explain launch risk.
output_examples.output: Verdict: Ready with fixes. SEO metadata passes key checks, but console errors and low contrast on secondary controls should be fixed before launch.

best_practices: Provide the target URL, viewport widths, auth state, and highest value user flows.
Run available automated checks, then verify failures in the rendered browser.
Mark skipped manual checks as residual risk instead of implying full coverage.
anti_patterns: Claiming WCAG compliance from automated scores alone.
Reporting vague issues without an affected element, evidence, or fix.
Auditing only source files when rendered browser behavior is available.

faq.question: Does this skill prove WCAG compliance?
faq.answer: No. It supports browser-based checks, but formal WCAG compliance needs a complete accessibility audit.

faq.question: Can it audit local or preview URLs?
faq.answer: Yes, when the current environment can access the URL and browser tooling is available.

faq.question: Does it require Lighthouse?
faq.answer: No. It prefers Lighthouse when available, but it can continue with browser-visible checks and note the limitation.

faq.question: What should I provide before an audit?
faq.answer: Provide the URL, viewports, auth state, priority flows, and any release criteria that matter.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated workflows?
faq.answer: Yes, if you provide safe access and clear instructions for the workflow to inspect.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: Findings are sorted by user impact and release risk, from deploy blockers to backlog improvements.
